model_fitness.best_available_model: Symptomatic heterozygous MeCP2+/- female mice (the mosaic genotype matching human Rett), dosed intranasally post-onset — the exact design already used for painless NGF mutein (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 37633263). Secondary model: Mecp2-null male mice for survival/brainstem severity, and patient-derived fibroblasts/neurons for Trk-pathway engagement.
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: Partially. The model has reduced BDNF/NGF-axis tone and arrested neuronal maturation without degeneration (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 40673967), and responds to a neurotrophin biologic post-onset (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 37633263). It does NOT model human-scale intranasal biodistribution: a mouse nose-to-brainstem distance is ~1-2 cm versus ~10 cm in humans (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID 37633263 — exposure uniformity not measured there).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes for Trk-expressing cortical/hippocampal neurons, GABAergic interneurons, basal forebrain cholinergic neurons and brainstem respiratory nuclei — all present and affected in Mecp2+/- mice (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 40673967).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Regional Trk phosphorylation (pTrkA/pTrkB, pAKT, pERK) by region-resolved immunoassay; whole-body plethysmography apnoea index; soma size and dendritic complexity; survival. Prior work in this model used survival and behaviour (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 37633263).
model_fitness.important_limitations: Behavioural rescue can occur in Mecp2+/- mice with persistent prefrontal/anterior cingulate projection abnormalities (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID 40673967), so mouse behaviour alone is a weak predictor; and the comparator that matters clinically (approved trofinetide, NCT04776746) has no established mouse-model benchmark, so superiority cannot be judged in this model.

plan.critical_question: Does intranasally delivered neurotrophin biologic actually engage Trk receptors in the brainstem respiratory/autonomic nuclei that drive human morbidity — or only in olfactory bulb and rostral cortex? This is the biggest unknown and is answerable before any further efficacy work.
plan.proposed_experiment: Single pharmacodynamic biodistribution/target-engagement study in symptomatic MeCP2+/- females (and Mecp2-null males for severity). Dose intranasal painless NGF mutein (hNGF-P61S/R100E-type) at the published efficacious dose plus 3x and 0.3x. At fixed times post-dose, microdissect olfactory bulb, frontal cortex, hippocampus, cerebellum and brainstem (nTS/pre-Botzinger) and quantify (a) mutein concentration by targeted LC-MS or ELISA and (b) pTrkA/pTrkB, pAKT, pERK normalised to total receptor, with a p75/Trk-inhibitor arm for epistasis. Run a parallel functional arm: whole-body plethysmography apnoea index before and after acute dosing in the same animals. Total n ~8/group; no new model construction needed.
plan.model: Symptomatic MeCP2+/- female mice (primary) + Mecp2-null males; intranasal route as in PMID 37633263.
plan.primary_readout: Brainstem-to-olfactory-bulb ratio of drug concentration and of Trk-pathway phosphorylation, plus acute change in plethysmographic apnoea index.
plan.supportive_result: Dose-dependent, inhibitor-sensitive Trk pathway phosphorylation in brainstem at >=20-30% of the olfactory-bulb level at a tolerated dose, accompanied by a measurable fall in apnoea index. Decision: advance to a chronic head-to-head versus trofinetide with apnoea/autonomic endpoints as the primary, differentiating outcome.
plan.negative_result: Drug and phospho-signal confined to olfactory bulb/rostral cortex with no brainstem Trk engagement, or apnoea index unchanged despite behavioural effects. Decision: deprioritise intranasal neurotrophin protein for the respiratory/autonomic morbidity claim; the only remaining path would be a BBB-shuttle-fused (transferrin/CD98-receptor) Trk biologic given systemically, re-tested on the same readout, and the behavioural-only benefit should not be pursued against an approved trophic agent.
plan.decision_enabled: Whether to invest in a second-generation neurotrophin biologic at all, and if so whether to keep the intranasal route or switch to a BBB-shuttle systemic format — decided on target engagement rather than on a composite behavioural endpoint that PMID 40673967 shows can move without circuit correction (EVIDENCE, contradictory).

model_fitness.best_available_model: Two-tier: (1) primary Mecp2-null and Mecp2+/- mouse neurons/acute slices with quantitative, orthogonal TrkB-activation assays (e.g. NanoBRET/HTRF pTrkB in TrkB-expressing reporter cells plus native neurons), with ANA-12/K-252a epistasis — the assay configuration already used phenotypically in PMID 37986936; (2) in vivo Mecp2+/- females with plethysmography, the configuration that generated the respiratory rescue claims (EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 22302819; PMID 25147297).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_mechanism: The disease mechanism, yes (reduced BDNF in Mecp2-deficient mouse brain and human Rett autopsy tissue; EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 37986936). The drug mechanism, no — whether LM22A-4/7,8-DHF are genuine TrkB agonists is unresolved. A targeted search for the published pharmacological challenge to these compounds returned no such paper (retrieved: only an unrelated cardiac LM22A-4 study, PMID 36884028), so the contradictory claim remains unverified in either direction (INFERENCE, inconclusive, PMID 36884028). Pleiotropy is independently indicated by 7,8-DHF effects in placenta and cardiomyocyte mitochondria (INFERENCE, contradictory, PMID 36764626; PMID 28677406).
model_fitness.captures_relevant_cell_type: Yes — CA1 pyramidal neurons (spine density response to LM22A-4, EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 37986936) and brainstem nTS respiratory neurons (hyperexcitability normalised, EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 25147297).
model_fitness.measurable_phenotype: Quantitative pTrkB(Y706/707, Y816)/total TrkB dose-response with Emax relative to recombinant BDNF; loss of effect in TrkB-knockdown neurons; ANA-12 shift. In vivo: apnoea index, spine density.
model_fitness.important_limitations: Phospho-TrkB western blots in tissue are the historic source of irreproducibility; the study must be powered, blinded, use a BDNF reference curve and a TrkB-null/knockdown negative control, otherwise it will not settle the question. Mouse behavioural composites are a poor translational surrogate (EVIDENCE, contradictory, PMID 40673967).

plan.critical_question: Are LM22A-4 and 7,8-DHF genuine TrkB agonists at brain-achievable exposures, or is the Mecp2 rescue off-target pharmacology? Nothing downstream — chemistry, dose, biomarker — can be designed until this is answered.
plan.proposed_experiment: Blinded, orthogonal target-deconvolution package, cheap and fast: (a) full concentration-response of LM22A-4 and 7,8-DHF versus recombinant BDNF in a quantitative TrkB-activation assay (NanoBRET or HTRF pTrkB) in TrkB-expressing cells and in primary Mecp2-null cortical neurons; (b) repeat in TrkB-knockdown/knockout neurons — a true agonist effect must vanish; (c) ANA-12 and K-252a epistasis at matched exposures; (d) measure free brain concentration at the in vivo efficacious dose and check it exceeds the in vitro EC50; (e) if phenotypic rescue persists in TrkB-null neurons, run unbiased chemoproteomics/kinome profiling to identify the real target. In parallel and independently, treat low-dose ketamine (approved, CNS-penetrant, BDNF/TrkB-linked; EVIDENCE, supportive, PMID 40612906) as the cheapest clinical probe of the BDNF/TrkB branch, using apnoea and arousal readouts measurable within days — the prior Rett ketamine trial stopped for funding, not futility (EVIDENCE, inconclusive, NCT02562820).
plan.model: TrkB reporter cells + primary Mecp2-null and wild-type mouse cortical neurons with TrkB knockdown controls; free-brain-concentration PK in Mecp2+/- mice.
plan.primary_readout: pTrkB EC50/Emax versus BDNF, abolition in TrkB-knockdown neurons, and free brain concentration / EC50 ratio at the efficacious in vivo dose.
plan.supportive_result: Reproducible, TrkB-dependent, ANA-12-shiftable pTrkB activation with free brain exposure above EC50. Decision: the target is pharmacologically valid — invest in TrkB partial-agonist chemistry with pTrkB as the dose-selection biomarker, and design the pivotal animal study around brainstem apnoea (the morbidity driver and the trofinetide-differentiating endpoint), not behavioural composites.
plan.negative_result: No concentration-dependent pTrkB signal, or phenotypic effects preserved in TrkB-knockdown neurons, or free brain exposure far below EC50. Decision: stop all TrkB-agonist chemistry immediately; redirect to (i) chemoproteomic identification of the actual mediator of the published Mecp2 rescue, which may be a better target, and (ii) the IGF-1/trophic branch, the only branch with an approved product (EVIDENCE, supportive, NCT04776746). Do not progress a compound whose SAR would track an unknown off-target.
plan.decision_enabled: Go/no-go on any new TrkB chemistry investment, and which trophic branch (TrkB versus IGF-1 versus repurposed ketamine) receives funding. A negative result saves a multi-year medicinal-chemistry programme and is the single highest-value experiment in this approach.
